'''Volodymyr Volodymyrovych Nemoshkalenko''' ({{Langx|uk|Володимир Володимирович Немошкаленко}}; 26 March 1933 – 25 June 2002) was a Soviet and Ukrainian [[physicist]], full member ([[academician]]) of the [[National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine]] (1982). He was best known for the development and application of methods of [[computational physics]] in the [[Solid-state physics|solid state]] [[spectroscopy]] and, in particular, for the discovery of the phenomenon of inoxidability of simple forms of matter on the surface of the [[Astronomical object|celestial bodies]].

== Biography ==
In 1956, he graduated from the [[Igor Sikorsky Kyiv Polytechnic Institute|Kyiv Polytechnic Institute]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Випускники кафедри – академіки та члени кореспонденти нану, які закінчили кафедру фізики металів |url=http://www.cad.ntu-kpi.kiev.ua/KPI/dep/mph/grad.uk.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140811232152/http://www.cad.ntu-kpi.kiev.ua/KPI/dep/mph/grad.uk.html |archive-date=2014-08-11 |access-date=2024-02-09 |website=cad.ntu-kpi.kiev.ua}}</ref> From 1956 he worked at the [[Kurdyumov Institute of Metal Physics|Institute of Metal Physics]] of NAS of Ukraine (since 1963&nbsp;– head of department, since 1967&nbsp;– Deputy Director of the institute, since 1989&nbsp;– Director).<ref>[http://www.imp.kiev.ua/ G.V. Kurdjumov Institute of Metal Physics]</ref>

His main achievements are associated with the development of physical basis of spectroscopic methods, which allowed to obtain reliable information about the [[electronic structure]] and electronic properties of materials, and in merging the [[electron spectroscopy]] experiment with the electronic band structure calculations—the two research directions which he had founded in the Institute of Metal Physics.<ref>[http://eses13.imp.kiev.ua V. V. Nemoshkalenko Memorial Conference and Workshop Electronic Structure and Electron Spectroscopies (ES&ES 2013)]</ref> V.V. Nemoshkalenko is co-discoverer of the phenomenon of inoxidability of simple forms of matter on the surface of the celestial bodies.

He died in [[Kyiv]] at the age of 69.

*[[USSR State Prize]], 1985

*[[State Prize of Ukraine]], 1992, 2002
